query: Using the reported HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy as the starting material and its quasi-static properties—786 MPa yield strength, 1314 MPa compressive strength, and 13.5% fracture strain—as the baseline, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to overcome limited strain hardening, poor uniform deformability, and rapid failure as strain rate increases under adiabatic dynamic deformation? Specify the intervention and mechanism, predict changes relative to the baseline in strength, uniform deformation, localization resistance, and impact-induced energy release, define the strain-rate and loading conditions over which the prediction applies, cite supporting evidence from the reported refractory-alloy literature, and describe a matched baseline-versus-intervention experiment that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of boron atoms or boride precipitates in the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy will enhance its mechanical properties by promoting short-range order, retarding dislocation motion, and increasing dislocation density, thereby overcoming the limitations of limited strain hardening, poor uniform deformability, and rapid failure under adiabatic dynamic deformation.
generation.material_initial_state: HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy with 786 MPa yield strength, 1314 MPa compressive strength, and 13.5% fracture strain
generation.intervention: Introduction of boron atoms or boride precipitates
generation.conditions: Adiabatic dynamic deformation at various strain rates
generation.mechanism: Retardation of dislocation motion and increase in dislocation density
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced yield strength, improved uniform deformability, and increased resistance to localization and impact-induced energy release
generation.baseline: 786 MPa yield strength, 1314 MPa compressive strength, and 13.5% fracture strain
generation.boundary: Strain rates ranging from 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of boron atoms or boride precipitates required to achieve optimal mechanical properties is uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties of the HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy with and without boron atoms or boride precipitates under adiabatic dynamic deformation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of boron atoms or boride precipitates does not result in significant improvements in mechanical properties, the hypothesis is falsified

We hypothesized that controlled additions of Al and Ti to the base CoFeNi random solid solution can introduce and progressively increase the extent of local chemical ordering, thereby modifying its mechanical response. Our hypothesis was tested via detailed investigations in four different alloys—CoFeNi (33Co-33Fe-33Ni at.%), Al0.25CoFeNi (7.6Al-30.8Co-30.8Fe-30.8Ni at.%), Al0.3CoFeNi (9.1Al-30.3Co-30.3Fe-30.3Ni at.%), and Al0.3Ti0.2CoFeNi (8.5Al-5.7Ti-28.6Co-28.6Fe-28.6Ni at.%). The compositions were chosen such that the transition from SRO tendency to fully developed long-range order (LRO) can be examined. These alloys were first homogenized and solution treated at 1,200 °C for 5 min within the single FCC phase field and then water-quenched to room temperature. The temperature was chosen based on the pseudobinary isopleths obtained from solution thermodynamic modeling (SI Appendix, Fig. S1). Further details regarding the basis of selection of alloy compositions are provided in SI Appendix. For single-phase solid-solution RHEAs, although the mechanical properties may be improved by the adjustment of the compositions, the strength–ductility trade-off problem remains [], and the development of other robust RHEAs is still demanded.
In recent years, heterostructural HEAs with microstructural heterogeneity to generate plastic discontinuity and thus mechanical strengthening have been intensively developed for overcoming the strength–ductility trade-off problem [,,,]. The proposed heterostructures include multiphase (most often called complex concentrated alloys), eutectic dual-phase and single-phase (grain-size gradient) structures [,,].
